As a credit rating analyst, the key metrics indicate severe financial distress. The current ratio of 0.42 is critically low, signaling acute liquidity issues and an inability to meet short-term obligations. The debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 10.25 (total liabilities / shareholders' equity = 3,107,151M / 303,243M), indicating extreme leverage, while the EBIT to total liabilities ratio is only 0.4% (12,435M / 3,107,151M), suggesting insufficient earnings to cover interest expenses. Despite a healthy EBIT margin of 25%, the low revenue relative to the balance sheet size (asset turnover of 1.46%) and negative working capital (-1,492,522M) point to high bankruptcy risk, supported by an estimated Altman Z-score of approximately -0.33. This combination of poor liquidity, unsustainable leverage, and low coverage ratios places the issuer in the very high-risk category.

DECISION: CCC
